video.title: Board of Trustees of the Affordable Housing Trust (AHT) 9/23/26

summary.headline: The Southborough Affordable Housing Trust refined housing survey questions, reviewed landowner outreach flyers, and explored higher-yield investment options for its funds.
summary.summary: The Affordable Housing Trust reviewed insights from a recent discussion with the Westborough Affordable Housing Trust and a presentation from affordable housing developer Penrose. Trustees discussed updates to a proposed 55-plus housing bylaw and revised housing-related questions for an upcoming townwide satisfaction survey. Members also reviewed drafts of an outreach brochure encouraging private land donations and agreed to investigate moving roughly $1 million in trust funds into interest-bearing investments.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The board approved minutes from open and executive sessions of August 26, confirmed its next meeting date, and adjourned the meeting.
key_details: Open session and executive session minutes from August 26 were approved unanimously.
The board scheduled its next regular meeting for October 28 at 7:30 p.m.

topics.title: Update on meeting with Westborough Affordable Housing Trust
topics.summary: Trustees reported on a meeting with the chair of the Westborough Affordable Housing Trust. They discussed Westborough's experience managing substantial developer mitigation payments, public outreach strategies, and partnerships with their local housing authority.
key_details: Westborough has amassed approximately $11 million from developers in lieu of building units or through mitigation agreements.
Westborough had twice fallen below the state Chapter 40B 10 percent affordable housing threshold, which impacted local school enrollment and prompted new school construction.
Trustees discussed Westborough's coordination with its housing authority and noted Southborough Housing Authority has contracted management services to the Framingham Housing Authority.
topics.outcome: Discussion only; members agreed to reach out to the Southborough Housing Authority chair for potential collaboration.

topics.title: 55-plus housing bylaw update
topics.summary: A trustee provided an update on drafting revisions to the 55-plus housing bylaw following consultations with planning staff and Zoning Board of Appeals support. The trust is working toward a draft that can be reviewed by town counsel and submitted to Annual Town Meeting.
key_details: Revisions incorporate public hearing feedback gathered during the previous winter.
Trustees plan to have an updated draft ready for review at their next meeting.
The target is to place the bylaw before voters at the 2025 Annual Town Meeting.
topics.outcome: Drafting ongoing; revised version to be presented at the October meeting.

topics.title: CHAPA leadership program and developer presentation
topics.summary: A trustee shared highlights from the Citizens' Housing and Planning Association (CHAPA) leadership cohort, including a presentation by Penrose, a regional affordable housing developer. Penrose discussed typical financing models, municipal partnerships, and development timelines.
key_details: Penrose generally targets 100 percent affordable developments of roughly 60 units to utilize low-income housing tax credits and state subsidies.
Projects typically serve households earning between 30 and 80 percent of Area Median Income (AMI).
Typical timelines run 3 to 4 years from site identification to project completion.
Developer noted that private land transfers simplify the process compared to public RFPs required for municipal land.
topics.outcome: Information shared with the trust for future planning.

topics.title: Town satisfaction survey housing questions review
topics.summary: The trust reviewed draft survey questions on affordable housing prepared for the Municipal Technology Committee's townwide satisfaction survey. Members discussed clarifying question wording, replacing confusing architectural terms, and adjusting demographic categories.
key_details: Trustees recommended replacing 'two-to-three story higher density developments' with simpler phrasing like 'two-to-three story developments'.
Members recommended clarifying 'workforce housing' to specify housing affordable for middle-income workers, including town employees and young families.
Question 68 was recommended to ask about housing in the downtown area rather than near the transfer station.
Trustees asked that multiple-choice questions clearly state 'check all that apply'.
topics.outcome: Comments and revisions will be submitted to the chair of the Municipal Technology Committee.

topics.title: Trust financing and investment options
topics.summary: The trust announced it received a state Mini-Boost technical assistance grant and submitted a Community Preservation Act (CPA) funding application. Members also discussed investing approximately $1 million of trust cash currently sitting in near-zero interest accounts into higher-yield instruments.
key_details: The trust received a Mini-Boost grant providing two staff members to assist with trust work.
A CPA funding application was submitted to the Community Preservation Committee.
The trust holds roughly $1 million in a bank account earning virtually zero interest.
A member calculated that the trust has forgone substantial six-figure earnings over 25 years by not investing the cash.
Trustees plan to consult town finance officials regarding legal options such as CD ladders or third-party management.
topics.outcome: A member agreed to follow up with the finance director regarding allowable investment vehicles.
topics.why_it_matters: Investing roughly $1 million in trust capital into higher-yield accounts could generate tens of thousands of dollars annually for affordable housing initiatives without additional taxpayer expense.

topics.title: Landowner donation outreach flyers
topics.summary: Trustees reviewed draft informational flyers aimed at property owners explaining the financial, tax, and community benefits of donating or selling land at a discount to the Affordable Housing Trust. Members debated distribution avenues, including Heritage Day, Town Meeting, and the senior center.
key_details: Flyers outline options including outright gifts, bargain sales, partial parcel gifts, and retained life estates.
Members agreed tax language should remain general until vetted by a certified public accountant.
Trustees discussed distributing a concise one-page summary to raise awareness among residents and local landowners.
topics.outcome: Members will seek tax review from a professional before finalizing the flyers.

topics.title: Potential parcels for acquisition
topics.summary: Trustees briefly reviewed potential land parcels for affordable housing development. One previously considered parcel was dropped after finding it is subject to a conservation restriction, while research continues on a municipal water tank parcel.
key_details: A parcel previously under consideration was removed from the list due to an existing conservation restriction.
The trust is continuing to coordinate with town staff regarding the Atwood Street water tank property and an adjacent parcel.
topics.outcome: Follow-up will continue on the Atwood Street property; no executive session was needed.
